mainTopic: Whether two people who bring a גט from overseas must say 'בפנינו נכתב ובפנינו נחתם', and the dispute of רבנן and רבי יהודה behind it.
overview: רב שמואל בר יהודה reports רבי יוחנן's ruling in two opposite versions. In the first version, a גט handed over by both bringers is valid, so two people who bring a גט from overseas do not need to say 'בפנינו נכתב ובפנינו נחתם'. In that version, רבנן invalidate a split testimony only as a גזירה, so people will not think ordinary documents can be confirmed by one witness. In the second version, רבנן invalidate the גט even when both hand it over. Here רבנן and רבי יהודה argue about the reason for the declaration: לשמה or קיום. The גמרא asks whether this makes the dispute of רבה and רבא a dispute of תנאים. It shows that each of them can fit both sides. רבה explains the argument as a גזירה in case people forget the law after they learned it. Next comes a challenge from the רישא, answered by עולא, and an objection from a ברייתא, which is also resolved. Finally רב יהודה supports the second version, and a story begins in which רבה בר בר חנה rules that two bringers do not need the declaration.

steps.title: Two people bringing a גט need not make the declaration
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes רבי יוחנן's ruling (valid when both hand over the גט) and concludes that two people who bring a גט from overseas do not need to say 'בפנינו נכתב ובפנינו נחתם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is valid. So it seems רבי יוחנן holds that two people who bring a גט from overseas do not have to say 'It was written in our presence and signed in our presence.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יוחנן's statement: if the גט comes out from the hands of both people, it is valid. Then it draws a general rule from that statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two people deliver the גט together, they are two full witnesses, and that already counts as proper קיום of the document. So the special declaration 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם', which is needed for a single שליח, is not needed when there are two.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid
Apparently / so we see that
A country overseas, outside ארץ ישראל
'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence', the declaration made by someone bringing a גט from overseas

steps.whyThisMatters: This conclusion is the basis for אביי's challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: it is valid.
Apparently, he holds
that two people who brought a bill of divorce from a country overseas
are not required to say:
"It was written in our presence and it was signed in our presence."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's statement, which began before this section, and draws an inference from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people who bring a גט from overseas do not need to declare 'בפנינו נכתב ובפנינו נחתם'.

steps.title: אביי challenges from the סיפא of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי points to the סיפא: two say 'written before us' and one says 'signed before me' is invalid. By רבי יוחנן's logic, if both handed over the גט, רבנן would call it valid. Is that really so?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But if so, look at the latter clause, which teaches: if two say 'It was written in our presence' and one says 'It was signed in my presence', it is invalid, and רבי יהודה says it is valid. According to you, the only reason it is invalid is that the גט did not come out from both of their hands. So if it did come out from both of their hands, would רבנן really call it valid?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the idea that two bringers never need the declaration. He applies it to the סיפא of the משנה and gets a result that sounds surprising.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule means the problem in these cases is only that the גט was not delivered by two. So in the סיפא, if the גט were delivered by both, רבנן would have to agree it is valid, even though the משנה just says 'פסול' without any such condition. אביי finds that hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, now (introduces a challenge from the consequences of an idea)
The latter clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Invalid
Deems valid
Comes out from under both of their hands, meaning both of them hand it over together

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב שמואל בר יהודה, who reported רבי יוחנן's ruling.

phrases.english: But if that is so,
the latter clause, which teaches:
if two say: "It was written in our presence"
and one says: "It was signed in my presence", it is invalid,
and Rabbi Yehuda deems it valid;

phrases.aramaic: טַעְמָא דְּאֵין הַגֵּט יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יְדֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם,
phrases.english: the reason is that the bill of divorce was not produced by both of them,

phrases.aramaic: הָא גֵּט יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יְדֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם –
phrases.english: but if the bill of divorce was produced by both of them,
would the Rabbis deem it valid?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference drawn in step 1 by applying it to the סיפא of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that two bringers need no declaration, and that רבי יוחנן's condition applies to the סיפא too.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If this were true, רבנן would call the סיפא's case valid whenever both hand over the גט, yet the משנה just calls it פסול without any condition.

steps.title: Yes, רבנן would call it valid
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה accepts the consequence: if the גט comes out from both of their hands, even רבנן agree it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר יהודה answers אביי with one word: 'Yes.' He accepts the conclusion אביי thought was strange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of defending against the challenge, he agrees with what it implies. The משנה's 'פסול' in the סיפא is understood as talking only about a case where the גט was not delivered by both, just like רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

steps.confusionAlert: 'אין' here is Aramaic for 'yes', not the Hebrew 'אֵין' meaning 'there is not'.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by accepting its consequence.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the challenge's consequence: the surprising result is actually correct.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי assumed רבנן would call the סיפא invalid in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן invalidate it only when the גט is not handed over by both. If both hand it over, it is valid.

steps.title: What is the disagreement about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: when the גט is not handed over by both, what is the reason רבנן and רבי יהודה disagree?
steps.simpleTranslation: And when the גט does not come out from both of their hands, what do they disagree about?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the argument is only about a case where both did not hand over the גט, the גמרא asks for the reasoning behind each side. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that case there are two witnesses for the writing but only one for the signing. The גמרא wants to know why רבנן reject this and why רבי יהודה accepts it.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי אֵין גֵּט יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יְדֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם
phrases.english: And when the bill of divorce was not produced by both of them,
about what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having limited the disagreement to a case where both did not hand over the גט, the גמרא asks for its reasoning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind the disagreement between רבנן and רבי יהודה when the גט is not handed over by both.

steps.title: A גזירה about ordinary document ratification
steps.stepSummary: רבנן make a גזירה so that people will not think ordinary documents can be ratified by one witness. רבי יהודה does not make this גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds: we make a decree, because people may confuse this with ordinary ratification of documents and think it can be done with one witness. And the other Sage holds: we do not make that decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the argument is about whether to make a protective decree (a גזירה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן worry that if a גט is accepted with only one person testifying about the signing, people will think any document can be ratified by a single witness. Normal קיום שטרות needs two witnesses. רבי יהודה holds there is no need for that worry, so he accepts the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: One Sage holds
We make a protective decree (גזירה)
Lest it come to be confused
Ratifying legal documents by confirming the signatures
One witness

steps.whatToRemember: When the גט is handed over by both bringers, it is valid even for רבנן. When it is not, רבנן invalidate it as a גזירה so people do not think documents can be ratified by one witness. רבי יהודה does not make this גזירה.

phrases.english: One Sage holds: we decree
phrases.notes: The first "מר" is רבנן, and the second one is רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: lest people come to confuse it
with the typical ratification of documents, and ratify them with one witness;
and one Sage holds: we do not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is about a גזירה: רבנן decree against it so people will not think documents can be ratified by one witness. רבי יהודה does not decree.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement is not about the basic law of the גט but about whether to make a protective decree tied to ordinary קיום שטרות.

steps.title: Second version: even from both hands the גט is invalid
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב שמואל בר יהודה reports that רבי יוחנן said the גט is invalid even when both messengers hand it over. The גמרא concludes that two messengers must also say 'בפנינו נכתב ובפנינו נחתם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some report it differently: רב שמואל בר יהודה said in the name of רבי יוחנן that even when the גט comes out of the hands of both of them, it is invalid. So it seems he holds that two people who bring a גט from overseas must say 'It was written before us and signed before us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second version of the earlier discussion, and in this version רבי יוחנן rules the opposite way from the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, a גט handed over by both messengers was valid, so two messengers did not need the declaration. In this version, רבי יוחנן says that even when both hand it over, רבנן invalidate it. The גמרא draws the conclusion (אלמא) that even two messengers must say the full declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of how the discussion went
Apparently, so we see (introduces a conclusion drawn from what was just said)
A country overseas, outside ארץ ישראל
The גט comes out of the hands of both of them, meaning both messengers hand it over together

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first version, a גט handed over by both messengers is valid. In this second version, it is invalid. Keep them as two separate tracks.

phrases.english: Some say it in another version:
Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda said,
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ גֵּט יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יְדֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם – פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: Even a get that comes out of the hands of both of them is invalid.
Apparently he holds
that two who brought a get from overseas
must say: 'It was written before us and it was signed before us.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the discussion from step 1 as a second version, with רבי יוחנן ruling the opposite way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a גט handed over by both messengers is invalid in the opinion of רבנן, so two messengers from overseas must also say 'בפנינו נכתב ובפנינו נחתם'.

steps.title: אביי asks: do רבנן really invalidate it even from both hands?
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes the סיפא, where רבנן invalidate the case of two who saw the writing and one who saw the signing. He asks whether רבנן really invalidate the גט even when both messengers hand it over.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, take the last part of the משנה, which teaches: two say 'it was written before us' and one says 'it was signed before me', it is invalid, and רבי יהודה says it is valid. Do רבנן really invalidate it even when the גט comes out of the hands of both of them?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tests the new version against the סיפא of the משנה and expresses surprise that רבנן would invalidate the גט even in such a strong case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both messengers hand over the גט, there are two witnesses to the writing, and one of them also saw the signing. That seems like plenty of testimony. אביי finds it hard to believe that רבנן would still call it invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then... (introduces a difficult consequence of what was just said)
The last clause of the משנה
Rules it valid
רבנן rule it invalid

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: But if so,
the latter clause, which teaches:
two say: 'It was written before us,'
and one says: 'It was signed before me,' it is invalid,
and Rabbi Yehuda deems it valid;

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ גֵּט יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יְדֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם
phrases.english: even when the get comes out of the hands of both of them
do the Rabbis invalidate it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second version of רבי יוחנן's ruling using the סיפא of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling, in the second version, that רבנן invalidate the גט even when both messengers hand it over.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With two witnesses to the writing, and one of them also present at the signing, it seems unreasonable for רבנן to invalidate the גט.

steps.title: Answer: yes, רבנן invalidate it
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה answers simply: yes, רבנן invalidate it even then.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר יהודה accepts אביי's point head-on and says that, yes, רבנן invalidate it even when both messengers hand it over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of looking for a way out, he accepts the surprising result. This is the opposite of his answer in the first version (step 3), where he said even רבנן agree the גט is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes (Aramaic)

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by accepting its consequence.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the consequence of the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed unreasonable for רבנן to invalidate the גט when both messengers hand it over.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן do invalidate it even then. The reason will be explained in the next steps.

steps.title: What are רבנן and רבי יהודה arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle lies behind the disagreement between רבנן and רבי יהודה in this version.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next step by asking what reasoning divides רבנן and רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן invalidate the גט even when both messengers hand it over, and רבי יהודה validates it. The גמרא wants to know which underlying idea causes this split.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ruling is accepted, the גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that divides רבנן from רבי יהודה in the second version.

steps.title: Two different reasons for the declaration
steps.stepSummary: רבנן hold that the declaration is needed because people overseas are not experts in writing the גט לשמה. רבי יהודה holds that it is needed because there are no witnesses available to confirm the signatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds that the reason is that they are not experts in writing it for her sake. The other master holds that the reason is that there are no witnesses available to confirm it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sides disagree about the reason we require the declaration 'בפנינו נכתב ובפנינו נחתם' in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason is לשמה (רבנן), two messengers still need to testify that it was written and signed for her, so the declaration is required. If the reason is קיום, confirming the signatures (רבי יהודה), two messengers already make confirmation possible, so the declaration is not needed and the גט is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: For her sake, meaning the גט must be written specifically for this woman
Experts, people who know the laws
To confirm it, to verify the witnesses' signatures (קיום שטרות)
One master holds

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, רבנן base the declaration on לשמה, so even two messengers must say it. רבי יהודה bases it on קיום, so two messengers do not need it.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין לִשְׁמָהּ,
phrases.english: One master holds: because they are not experts in writing it for her sake,
phrases.notes: This first 'master' is רבנן, and the second is רבי יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עֵדִים מְצוּיִין לְקַיְּימוֹ.
phrases.english: and the other master holds: because there are no witnesses available to confirm it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן base the declaration on לשמה. רבי יהודה bases it on there being no witnesses available to confirm the signatures.

steps.title: Is the dispute of רבה and רבא really a dispute of תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: Since these two reasons are the same ones that רבה and רבא give, the גמרא suggests that רבה and רבא simply follow two sides of an earlier dispute between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that the dispute of רבה and רבא is the same as a dispute between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the two reasons match the earlier dispute of רבה and רבא, and suggests that their dispute is really the same as the תנאים' dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה holds that the declaration is because of לשמה, and רבא holds that it is because of קיום. If רבנן and רבי יהודה split on exactly these reasons, then each אמורא simply sides with one of the תנאים. The גמרא generally prefers not to say this, so it raises the idea in order to test it.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא wants to test)
It is a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: Shall we say that the dispute of Rabba and Rava is a dispute of tanna'im?
phrases.notes: This points back to the start of the מסכת, where רבה gave the לשמה reason and רבא gave the confirming reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a consequence from step 10 for the earlier dispute of the אמוראים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dispute of רבה and רבא is the same as the dispute of רבנן and רבי יהודה.

steps.title: No: רבא can follow the first version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. רבא explains the dispute according to the first version, where everyone agrees two messengers need no declaration, so his reason does not have to depend on one side of the תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. רבא explains it according to the first version.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion by saying that רבא does not have to accept the second version at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבנן agree that a גט handed over by both messengers is valid, so the תנאים do not split on the reasons. That way רבא's reason, קיום, fits everyone and does not make him side with only one תנא. The sentence continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains, resolves the text
The first version

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא avoiding turning a dispute of אמוראים into a dispute of תנאים, by choosing which version of the discussion each אמורא follows.

phrases.english: No;
Rava explains it according to the first version,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבא's position must depend on one side of a dispute between תנאים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumes the second version. רבא can follow the first version, in which the תנאים do not argue about the reason.

steps.title: רבה also does not need to depend on the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains the dispute so that everyone agrees with his reason of לשמה. They only argue about a גזירה for the time after people learned the law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה could say to you: everyone agrees that the declaration is needed because of לשמה. Here we are dealing with the time after they learned. They argue about a גזירה in case things go back to how they were. One side holds we make the גזירה, and the other holds we don't.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 12 showed that רבא's reason can fit everyone. Now the גמרא shows that רבה's reason of לשמה can also fit everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, both רבנן and רבי יהודה agree that the declaration was made because people overseas did not know about לשמה. The argument is only about the period after they learned. רבנן still require the declaration in case people forget, while רבי יהודה does not make that extra גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: After they learned, meaning after people overseas already knew to write a גט לשמה
A rabbinic safeguard decree
In case the matter goes back to its broken state, meaning people might forget the law
We make the decree

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה rejects the reason of לשמה. In this reading he agrees with it. He only disagrees about adding a גזירה after people already learned.

phrases.english: And Rabba could say to you:
Everyone agrees we require it because of "for her sake,"
phrases.notes: He means everyone agrees the declaration exists because people didn't know to write the גט for this specific woman.

phrases.english: and here, what are we dealing with?
After they learned.
And about a decree, in case it goes back
the matter to its broken state, they argue.
One master holds we decree,
phrases.notes: This is רבנן, who invalidate the גט.

phrases.english: and one master holds we do not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection begun in step 12 by doing the same thing for רבה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבה depends on one side of the תנאים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can be explained as being about a later גזירה, not about the basic reason for the declaration.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יהודה argue on the first case too?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה does not make the extra גזירה, he should also allow the first case of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let רבי יהודה also argue on the first case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case of the משנה, one messenger says it was written in front of him and the other says it was signed in front of him. If רבי יהודה does not make the גזירה, that case should be valid for him too. Yet the משנה only shows him arguing on the later case.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him argue
The first clause of the משנה

phrases.english: Then let Rabbi Yehuda also argue on the first clause!
phrases.notes: The first clause is the case where one says "written in my presence" and the other says "signed in my presence."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation of רבי יהודה's view given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רבי יהודה does not make the גזירה after people learned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that is his reason, it should also apply to the first case, but the משנה only shows him disagreeing on the later case.

steps.title: עולא: רבי יהודה argues on the first case too
steps.stepSummary: עולא already said that רבי יהודה disagrees even in the first case of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was already said about this: עולא said, רבי יהודה disagreed even on the first case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that רבי יהודה agrees in the first case. עולא says he does not agree there either. So רבי יהודה's view stays consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: It was already stated about it
Disagreeing
Even on the first case

phrases.english: It was already stated about it: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: חָלוּק הָיָה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַף בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda was disagreeing even on the first case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an earlier statement that widens רבי יהודה's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה disagrees only in the later case.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to עולא, רבי יהודה validates the גט in the first case too.

steps.title: רב אושעיא challenges עולא from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says רבי יהודה validates the גט in one case but not in another. That seems to exclude the first case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא challenged עולא: רבי יהודה validates in this case but not in another. Doesn't that mean to exclude the case where one says "it was written in front of me" and one says "it was signed in front of me"?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא attacks עולא's answer with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא limits רבי יהודה's ruling to one case. The simplest case to exclude is the first case of the משנה, which is exactly where עולא said רבי יהודה is lenient. If so, the ברייתא contradicts עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules it valid
To exclude
It was signed in front of me

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya objected to Ulla:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁיר בְּזוֹ וְלֹא בְּאַחֶרֶת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda validates in this case but not in another.
What, isn't it to exclude
where one says "it was written in my presence"
and one says "it was signed in my presence"?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of עולא given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that רבי יהודה disagrees even in the first case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says רבי יהודה validates only one case. The excluded case seems to be the first case, which goes against עולא.

steps.title: The ברייתא excludes a lone witness who saw only the signing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is not excluding the first case of the משנה. It excludes one witness who says the גט was signed, but not written, in front of him. רבי יהודה invalidates this for fear people will confuse it with קיום שטרות, which needs two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The ברייתא comes to exclude a case where one person says, "It was signed in front of me, but not written in front of me." You might have thought: רבי יהודה did not make a גזירה out of worry that things would go back to the old mistake. So maybe he also did not make a גזירה out of worry that people would confuse this with confirming ordinary documents through one witness. The ברייתא teaches us that he does make that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16. The case the ברייתא rules out is not the first case of the משנה. It is a different case: one witness who only saw the signing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "it was signed in front of me" is like confirming a document's signatures (קיום שטרות). That normally needs two witnesses, so רבי יהודה invalidates it when only one witness says it. The ברייתא needs to teach this because we might have thought that someone who skips one גזירה skips the other too.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to rule out a case
You might have thought to say
Lest the matter go back to its earlier broken state
Confirming the signatures on legal documents
One single witness
It teaches us (the opposite of what we might have thought)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two worries. רבי יהודה drops the worry that people will forget the law (step 13). He keeps the worry that people will confuse a גט with ordinary document confirmation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves עולא's claim from step 15. רבי יהודה can still disagree about the first case of the משנה, and the ברייתא does not contradict that.

phrases.english: No, it comes to exclude
"It was signed in my presence but not written in my presence"
It might enter your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְלָא גָּזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה גְּזֵירָה
phrases.english: Since רבי יהודה did not make a decree
lest the matter return to its broken state,
phrases.notes: This is the extra גזירה from step 13: the worry that people might forget the law again.

phrases.english: the decree that perhaps people will come to confuse it
with the confirming of ordinary documents,
with one witness, he also does not make;
phrases.notes: Ordinary documents can't be confirmed by just one witness, so that is the mix-up being worried about.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines which case the ברייתא excludes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא excludes the first case of the משנה. That would contradict עולא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא excludes one witness who saw only the signing. This is invalid because it could be confused with קיום שטרות.

steps.title: רב יהודה: Two messengers are the dispute of רבי יהודה and the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that two people who brought a גט from overseas fall into the dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן. This matches what was said earlier in another name.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said: רב יהודה said: When two people bring a גט from overseas, we have come to the dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אמורא who says the same thing that was said earlier. The case of two messengers depends on the argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "it was also said" shows that a second authority holds the same view. Whether two messengers must make the declaration is tied to that תנאים dispute. It is not something everyone agrees on.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (another authority says the same)
A land overseas, outside ארץ ישראל
A dispute

phrases.english: It was also stated: רב יהודה said:
Two who brought a גט from overseas,
we have come to the dispute of רבי יהודה and the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main question of two messengers. It brings רב יהודה as support for the second version of רבי יוחנן's ruling (step 6): even when two bring the גט, the case depends on the dispute of רבי יהודה and רבנן.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that two messengers fall into the dispute of רבי יהודה and the רבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A parallel statement of רב יהודה

steps.title: רב יהודה and רבה ask רבה בר בר חנה about two messengers
steps.stepSummary: While visiting רבה בר בר חנה when he was ill, רב יהודה and רבה ask him whether two messengers must say "it was written and signed in front of us."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה was ill. רב יהודה and רבה went in to visit him and ask how he was. They asked him: two people brought a גט from overseas. Do they need to say, "It was written in front of us and signed in front of us," or don't they?
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. Two sages visit a sick colleague and ask him the very question the גמרא has been discussing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the declaration בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם is needed only for one messenger, or for two messengers as well. This sets up a ruling from רבה בר בר חנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Became weak, was ill
To ask about his well-being
They asked him (a question of law)
It was written in our presence and signed in our presence

phrases.english: רבה בר בר חנה became ill,
רב יהודה and רבה went in to him,
to ask how he was.
They asked him:
Two who brought a גט from overseas,
do they need to say
"It was written in our presence and signed in our presence,"
or do they not need to?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that deals with the same question of two messengers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether two messengers must make the declaration בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם

steps.title: They need not, because two witnesses would be believed anyway
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה answers that two messengers don't need the declaration. Even if they said "he divorced her in front of us," they would be believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: They don't need to. If they said, "He divorced her in front of us," wouldn't they be believed?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה answers the question. Two messengers do not need to say the declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses are believed even if they testify directly that the divorce happened. So they certainly don't need the smaller declaration about how the גט was written and signed. Their being two witnesses is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: What if, suppose
He divorced her
They are believed, trusted

phrases.english: He said to them: They do not need to.
What if they would say "He divorced her in our presence":
would they not be believed?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two messengers don't need the declaration, since two witnesses would be believed even about the divorce itself.

steps.title: Meanwhile, someone walks in
steps.stepSummary: While they are sitting there, a certain person arrives. The story continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the meantime, a certain [person] came in.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The story is about to continue with someone new coming in, which leads to the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sentence stops in the middle here and continues on the next amud, where we find out who arrives and what happens.

keyTerms.meaning: In the meantime, while this was happening
A certain (person)

phrases.english: In the meantime,
a certain [person] came in

steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This is a story transition that sets up the next event.
